releases.notes:
Mostly repair work, finishing the meeting capture the last release started.

## Highlights

- :srcWave: **Wave meetings keep every word, and every voice** A recording could be stored missing a third of what was said, with its turns run together and unattributed. Both are fixed, and sessions already stored that way are re-read for you.
- :pencil: **Rename and pin without opening a conversation** Right-click any row or card in the Library. The new title now appears the moment you press Enter, instead of when the source gets round to confirming it.
- :chat: **Conversations open instantly** The Reader draws its real shape straight away and fills it in, rather than sitting blank and then telling you the conversation is not available while it is still looking.

> Wave summaries, lost titles, the update window

## Added

- **Rename** and **Pin** in the Library's right-click menu, in the list and the card view alike, above Add to Project and Delete. Rename turns the row's title, or the card's heading, into an editor in place. An action the source cannot take stays in the menu, disabled, with a tooltip saying why, and progress appears in the same corner cards a delete uses.

## Improved

- A rename shows its new title immediately, in the Library and in the Reader. It goes back to the old one only if the source refuses, with the status card saying why. Pushing a rename drives a browser in the background and takes around fifteen seconds on some sources, which read as the pencil having done nothing at all.
- Opening a conversation no longer means waiting on a blank window. The header, the toolbar and the message area are drawn before anything is requested, as placeholders the real content lands in without the page moving, and "Conversation not available" now appears only when the conversation really is gone.
- The update window reads in two tiers. The opening line and the release's two or three highlights come first, and everything else collapses into one row you can expand, labelled with what it covers. Releases you skipped read the same way, and Settings shows the same notes with the record already open. A release with no highlights shows its full record, as before.

## Fixed

- A Wave recording is stored with all of its words and with the speaker label Wave itself shows above each turn — a real name where its diarizer has one, Speaker 1 or Unknown Speaker where it does not. Turns are checked against the recording's own flat transcript before anything is stored, and where a passage cannot be put to a voice the words are kept without one rather than attributed to the wrong person.
- A Wave session no longer loses its transcript to a scrape that could read only the summary: it keeps the words it already had, and the Summary | Transcript switch stays where it was.
- Wave summaries are read from the session's own data rather than off the page, so a session cannot be caught mid-render or read out of the summary editor while it is open. A summary that comes back holding less than the one already stored is refused, and one holding more is always accepted, so a session stored short repairs itself the next time it is read.
- A scrape whose title read comes back empty leaves the stored title alone instead of erasing it. On every source: a conversation no longer goes untitled in the Library because one scrape missed a heading, and no longer drops out of search by name in the meantime.
- Speaker 1 and Unknown Speaker are no longer counted as people when the app works out who was in a meeting.

A big update, and the largest change to how meetings are stored so far.

## Highlights

- :srcWave: **Wave meetings keep the full transcript** Not just the summary — every turn, who said it, and when. Switch between Summary and Transcript in the Reader. All of it is searchable.
- :srcGemini: **Long Gemini conversations no longer shrink** Re-opening a chat used to save Gemini's shortened view over the full one. A re-scrape can now only ever add to what is stored — on every source.
- :file: **Recordings read as documents** One sheet across a wider page, instead of the chat bubbles a meeting never had.

> the update window, icons, prompt counts, Wave fixes

## Added

- Wave sessions now keep the full transcript, not just the summary. Where Wave separated the voices each turn is stored as who said it and what they said, with how far into the recording it was said; a session imported from a PDF or a YouTube video keeps the extracted document. Everything is searchable.
- A Summary | Transcript switch in the Reader on a Wave session. Summary opens first, each view scrolls from the top, and its copy button takes the whole of it. The switch appears only when the session actually holds both halves.
- A search result opens a Wave session on the half the match is in, instead of on the summary with the evidence off screen.
- The update window says where you stand under the new version's name — "You're on 0.1.85", and, when you skipped releases, that it also installs the ones in between.

## Improved

- A recorded session reads as a document. Summary and transcript are drawn as one sheet across a wider measure, without the chat bubbles and the source glyph beside every block, which made a meeting look like a conversation it never was. Find-in-conversation, the next-section button and search landing still move through it block by block.
- Wave summaries are kept as Wave wrote them: headings, bullets and bold intact, and nothing above the first heading dropped.
- Meeting sources no longer show a prompt count. A recording has no prompts; the number was only how the text had been cut up for search. Cards, rows and the Reader header leave the spot empty.
- Releases you skipped are now listed under "Also installed with this update", each as a collapsed row you can expand, with the new version's own notes always open. The footer states that ChatsRecall restarts to finish installing, and the window keeps keyboard focus inside it while Escape still closes it.
- Icons throughout the app are drawn with a heavier stroke, so they no longer read thin and washed out beside the text next to them.

## Fixed

- Re-opening a long Gemini conversation no longer shrinks it. Gemini only loads its most recent exchanges when you open a chat, and that shortened version was being stored over the full one; ChatsRecall now fetches the earlier exchanges itself, and a re-scrape can only ever add to what is stored. This applies to every source: a conversation already saved in full is never replaced by a shorter read of it.
- A Wave session no longer moves about between scrapes. A summary caught mid-render is recognized and ignored instead of overwriting the settled one, so the section count and the point where Summary ends and Transcript begins stay put. Sessions already stored from a half-rendered page are re-read once on the next sync; nothing has to be found by hand.
- An imported Wave session no longer stores its summary twice, once as the summary and again as the transcript.

A small release: quality-of-life work throughout, nothing new to learn.

## Highlights

- :sync: **A list that is still loading no longer says "nothing here"** Chats, Projects, Files and Extensions all show that they are still looking. Searching says so too, instead of flashing "No matching conversations" first.
- :help: **The guided tour was rebuilt** It now covers source filtering, Projects and opening a chat, and every step that had gone stale was rewritten.

> list view, file names, back links, hover hints

## Added

- A back link at the top of New Chat and Continue in another app. It returns to the conversation you were handing off, or to the project you started the chat for, and falls back to Chats otherwise. Escape does the same thing.
- List view shows files. A row with files carries the same chip the cards do, and a row without them gives the space back to the title.

## Improved

- Files, generated and attached are now the only words the app uses for them. The file chip reads "10 files" and the breakdown moved to the hover ("Files: 3 generated, 7 attached"), the file filter says "Any file", and the Files page marks each row Generated or Attached.
- A list that is still reading never looks like one that has answered. Loading is a dashed panel with the page's pulsing icon; an answer, including "nothing here", is a solid card. Chats, Projects, Files and Extensions all follow it.
- The Projects page shows that indicator for every read, not just the first one after startup, so it no longer says "No projects yet" while it is still looking. Projects already on screen stay put while the list refreshes.
- The Extensions count stays blank until the check for connected browsers answers, instead of reading 0 first.
- Hover hints now name the chips whose text is a bare value: the file count, the prompt count, and the folder, project, repository and branch tags.
- The prompt count spells the word out in both views, since the speech bubble on its own reads as messages just as easily.
- Claude Code chats no longer show the same folder twice. The repository tag already names the working directory, so the footer's folder chip is left off for them. A ChatsRecall project still shows.
- The guided tour was rebuilt against the current app. It now covers filtering by source and the three source settings, Projects, and opening a chat, and every step that had gone stale was rewritten.
- Help explains how to take a source out of the sidebar, and what the difference is between hiding its row and hiding its chats.
- Concepts, Entities and Moments are drawn with the app's standard controls: the same segmented switch, search fields, buttons and selection styling as the rest of the app.
- Pinned has finished moving out of the sidebar. The row is gone from every page; use Pinned only in Filters next to the search box.

## Fixed

- Release notes read as they were written. Bullets in the update window, in Settings, and on the website no longer break mid-sentence and leave a word stranded on its own line.
- Searching no longer flashes "No matching conversations" for a second before the results arrive. The list says it is searching until there is an answer.

Browse your chats by day, as cards or as a list, and hand a conversation to another app for a second opinion.

## Added

- List view is back. Switch between cards and a list with the buttons next to the page title. Each row shows the title and opening prompt on one line, with the project, prompt count and time beside them. Your choice is remembered.
- Chats are grouped by date: Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, then by month. New Chat is always the first item in Today.
- Continue in another app has two new modes. Give me a second opinion sends only your prompts, with the replies left out. Review this critically sends the whole conversation and asks what is wrong, weak, missing or risky in it.
- A short guided tour shows what changed the first time you open this version.

## Improved

- Pinned is now a filter. Turn on Pinned only in Filters, next to the search box, and combine it with a source, account, project or search to see, for example, only your pinned Gemini chats. It no longer takes a row in the sidebar.
- The search box buttons are labelled Ask and Filters.
- Cards are easier to scan. The date sits above the title where the source name used to be (the source icon still tells you where a chat is from), and inside Today and Yesterday it shows just the time. Previews that only repeat the title are hidden, and everything under the title lines up with it.
- The button next to Sources shows how many sources are hidden instead of a dot, and the sources window explains that hidden sources don't appear in Chats or search but keep syncing.
- Hover hints on icon buttons and cut-off names appear almost immediately and match the app's look.
- Continue in another app opens directly when only one browser extension can do it, and asks which browser to use otherwise. If the browser can't open it, the choice comes back with the reason.
- Handing off a conversation that was itself handed off no longer stacks instructions inside the title and prompts.

## Fixed

- Gemini conversations no longer miss prompts that were scrolled out of view, including turns that only contain an attachment.
- Deleting a conversation always removes it from ChatsRecall, even when a sync runs at the same moment.
- Continue in another app no longer mixes your text with a draft the other app restores in its message box. It waits for the box to settle and tells you if an earlier draft is still there.

Find any word inside a long conversation, and judge search results at a glance.

## Added

- Find in conversation. Press Ctrl+F in the Reader, or click the magnifier in its header, to search the conversation you are reading. Enter and Shift+Enter step through the matches with a count of where you are, and Esc closes the bar. Opened from a search result, it starts filled with your search.
- Sort Classic search by relevance. The Newest first / Relevance choice in the search options now works for Classic as well as Ladder.
- AI assistants connected through the local API or MCP can ask your archive a question and get a cited answer, the same one the Ask archive button gives. This needs a token with the new "ask" permission.

## Improved

- Search excerpts show more of the text around the match.
- Cards from today and yesterday show the time, such as "Today, 2:14 PM", so same-day conversations are easy to tell apart.
- New installs open in a larger window, and Settings > Reset UI > Minimize View returns to that size.

## Fixed

- Imported transcripts and Zoom meetings now show up in the library and in search. Before, they were saved but never shown.
- Opening a search result now highlights every match in the conversation and scrolls to the right one, including when you click anywhere on the card rather than on an excerpt.
- A result card with no matching excerpt no longer bolds unrelated words in its preview.

Delete a conversation once and it is gone from both places: its source and ChatsRecall. When the source cannot be reached right then, ChatsRecall removes it here and finishes the job at the source on a later sync.

## Added

- Delete at the source and here, together, so the two never disagree. The action is in the Library and in the Reader header, and the confirmation says which of the two it is about to do, because that depends on the source. Most sources delete at the source and the local copy goes with it. Wave, Read AI, Fireflies, Zoom, and Claude Code or Cowork sessions that live only on this computer have no delete ChatsRecall can reach, so the confirmation says so up front and offers to remove the conversation from ChatsRecall alone, leaving the original where it is.
- Delete now, remove at the source later. If the delete at the source fails, because nobody is signed into the right account, no browser is open, or the source itself is erroring, the status card offers to remove the conversation from ChatsRecall straight away and finish at the source on a later sync. That card waits for an answer instead of fading away.
- Syncs finish the deletes you queued. While that happens the source's row in the live view reads "Deleting" and names how many conversations are being removed at the source, counting through them when there is more than one. It returns to its normal finished state as soon as they are done, and a browser still working through them keeps its spinner until it has finished.
- A conversation you deleted never comes back. Syncing and live capture both check what you deleted before storing anything, so a chat that still exists at its source is not added again on the next sync. Wiping a source's local data from Settings clears that record too, so the source starts over completely.

## Improved

- Starting a new chat picks the right browser. With one compatible connector the tab opens immediately. With two or more, a dialog lists the connected browsers and you choose where the chat opens, rather than one being picked for you.
- Google AI Mode never offers a browser that cannot run it.
- The conversation you started opens by itself. Once its first message is captured and saved, ChatsRecall opens it in the Reader in the background. The browser keeps focus, so coming back to ChatsRecall shows the chat already open. If it belongs to a project it is filed there, with a "Saved to" toast when that project's list is on screen. This works with or without a project.
- A conversation you continue somewhere else comes back here on its own. Pick where to continue it, send when you are ready, and once the new conversation is captured ChatsRecall opens it in the Reader, again without taking the browser's focus. If the conversation you continued from belonged to a project, the continued chat is filed into the same project once it is sent, and both the page and the confirmation name that project. Nothing opens if you never send.
- The confirmation shown when a chat is launched explains what will happen: that you send when you are ready, and that the conversation will open here once it is saved. An empty tab or an unsent draft does not open anything, and Claude Code cloud says up front that it will not open here automatically.

## Fixed

- A queued delete that keeps failing is no longer retried forever. It is tried for ten syncs and then abandoned, and the Sync History row for that source says what succeeded and what was given up on.

Take a conversation with you: open it again in another app, already written into the message box.

## Added

- Continue in another app. The Reader has a new action next to Open Original. Pick where to continue and ChatsRecall opens a new chat there with the conversation already in the message box, as one draft. Nothing is sent: you read it over and press send yourself. Destinations are ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google AI Mode. Any conversation can be the starting point, including Cowork and Claude Code sessions that only exist on this computer.
- Hand over the whole conversation or a summary of it. The full transcript goes across as prompts and replies, capped at 50,000 characters: a longer conversation keeps its most recent messages and tells you how many earlier ones were left out. The summary is written by a model (the goal, what was decided, what is still open, where to pick up) and needs an OpenAI or Anthropic key in Settings; without one that choice is disabled with the reason on it.
- A conversation that belongs to a ChatsRecall project carries the project with it: the chat you continue is filed there as soon as you send it.

## Improved

- The browser connector's popup is a flat panel in the app's own colors now, following your system's light or dark setting. Connection status is one row that says what to do if it is down, sources waiting for a permission are plain rows with an Allow button, and the command history moved to a Logs link in the footer.
- A pasted-in conversation keeps its line breaks everywhere. Perplexity's message box used to fold the whole text into a single line, so it was offered only as a disabled destination; with browser extension 0.1.9 it keeps every line and blank line, and joins the list.

Rename a conversation in ChatsRecall and the source follows.

## Added

- Two-way renaming. The Reader's header has a rename action: click the pencil, type the new title, press Enter, and the conversation is renamed at its source. The title in your library only changes once the source confirms. Works for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Copilot, Wave, and Claude Code and Cowork cloud sessions. Where a source has no rename (Google AI Mode, meeting notetakers, imports, local Claude sessions), the action stays visible but disabled, with a tooltip saying why.
- Open at source from any message. Every prompt and response in the Reader has an action that opens the original conversation in your browser scrolled to that exact message, with the message outlined on the page.

## Fixed

- Wave favourites. Wave moved its favourite toggle into a "Session tools" dialog, which left favourite status stuck at "not favourited" for captured sessions and broke pinning from the app. Both follow the dialog now.

Start a chat straight from a project, and search stays fast while a sync runs.

## Added

- Inside a ChatsRecall project, a New Chat card leads the grid. The first conversation you start from it is saved to that project automatically, with a "Saved to <project>" confirmation.

## Improved

- Searching with Ladder no longer pauses to rebuild its indexes. New and changed conversations are indexed as they are saved, so a search stays quick even while a sync or backfill is running.
- New Chat opens the source in your primary connected browser and brings that window to the front. Google AI Mode picks the first browser allowed to run it.

## Fixed

- Clicking outside the search options popover only closes it; the sidebar row or conversation card under the pointer is no longer activated by that click.

Capture keeps up with the site changes that landed on Gemini, Perplexity, ChatGPT and Wave.

## Fixed

- Gemini prompts are saved the way you typed them. Prompts captured since late August were stored twice over, with a cut-off copy stuck to the front.
- Gemini conversation titles no longer contain stray " " text. Titles already saved that way are repaired on first launch.
- Perplexity prompts are captured again after Perplexity redesigned its conversation page.
- Deleting a Perplexity thread from ChatsRecall removes it on Perplexity again.
- Conversations you delete on ChatGPT are recognized again, so they no longer linger in your library.
- Wave conversations load their titles again instead of stalling on the way in.

Ask your archive handles long questions without stopping, and every answer shows what it cost.

## Added

- Every answer from Ask your archive shows the tokens the run used, what it cost, and how long it took.
- A thumbs up or thumbs down under each answer sends feedback on whether it was useful.

## Fixed

- Ask your archive no longer stops partway through a long question with a token budget error. When a run does reach its ceiling, it answers from the evidence it already gathered and tells you it finished early.

Syncing keeps your place in the list, and a few rough edges in the sidebar are gone.

## Improved

- Headings across the app use one consistent weight and letter spacing.

## Fixed

- Syncing no longer interrupts the conversation list. Conversations appear as they are saved, and the list keeps your scroll position instead of jumping back to the top.
- Changing a source's visibility quickly no longer leaves an empty row behind in the sidebar.
- "All Sources" no longer appears selected when no source filter is set.

Create your own projects that mix conversations from any source, and search options now live in one place.

## Added

- ChatsRecall projects: create a project inside the app and fill it with conversations from any mix of sources. Right-click a conversation card to add or move it, or use the folder button while reading a conversation. Projects live only in ChatsRecall: syncing never touches them, and deleting one never deletes any conversations.
- Claude Code sessions now group into folders by the repository they worked in, covering both cloud and local sessions.
- A short one-time walkthrough after this update points out where the search filters moved and how to create your first project.

## Improved

- The search field is now the single place for finding things. A sliders icon inside it opens the search options: the choice between Classic and Ladder search, Ladder's result sorting, and the file-type filter. A small dot on the icon shows when any of these is set away from the default. The sparkles button in the same field opens Ask your archive.
- Starting a new chat moved from the header button to a dashed card ahead of the first conversation.
- Conversation cards show a folder chip naming the project or folder they belong to.
- While a search is still running, a "Searching" indicator shows instead of claiming there are no results.
- The choices in the sources popover now explain themselves in short bullet points: what each visibility option hides, with the reminder that syncing never stops and no data is deleted.
- The filter button next to SOURCES shows a dot while any source is hidden, and the sidebar's conversation counts always match the conversations shown.

Source visibility now lives in one place, and the update window catches you up on releases you skipped.

## Added

- Sources popover: the filter button next to the SOURCES label now manages everything about source visibility in one place. Each source can be Shown, kept out of the sidebar only, or hidden from the library and search entirely, and you can drag sources into your own sidebar order. Hiding is display only: every source keeps syncing and its data stays put.

## Improved

- The update window now catches you up. If you skipped versions, it also shows the release notes for every update between your version and the new one, each under its own heading.
- The per-source library switches moved from Settings into the sources popover, so visibility lives in one place.

The sidebar is reorganized around a simpler idea: your content on top, the app itself in the footer.

## Added

- A one-time tip after updating highlights Sync's new home in the sidebar footer.

## Improved

- Sidebar navigation is grouped under small Library and Insights headers instead of divider lines.
- Sync moved to the sidebar footer next to Extensions, Settings, and Help: the corner where you take care of the app itself.
- Usage is now a tab on the Sync page instead of a separate page.
- The Sync page is lighter: the per-source library visibility switches moved to Settings, and bulk selection is a single button.
- The app name now leads the sidebar, with the collapse button on the right.

Search works again on installs where the Ladder engine had gone quiet.

## Fixed

- Ladder search returned zero results for every query on databases that skipped the search index build during an earlier upgrade. The missing indexes are now detected and rebuilt automatically on the next launch; the repair takes a few seconds on a large archive.
- Fireflies conversations were filtered out of the library pages. They now appear alongside every other source.

Pinning now reaches your Claude Code and Cowork sessions.

## Added

- Two-way pinning for Claude Code and Cowork cloud sessions. A session pinned on claude.ai shows as pinned in your library after a sync, and the Reader's pin button pins or unpins the session at claude.ai itself, through the same synced store the claude.ai sidebar reads. Pins made anywhere follow your account, not the browser they were made in.
- Pins on local sessions are captured too. A Claude Code or Cowork session pinned in the Claude desktop app on this computer arrives in your library as pinned on the next sync.
- Zoom appears in the sync source list. Connecting a Zoom account is not possible yet, so selecting the source finds nothing until that lands.

## Improved

- The Reader's pin button now explains itself on sessions whose pin the app cannot change, instead of attempting a push that cannot succeed: sessions that live on this computer point you to the Claude desktop app.

Your archive gains two indexes over what it already holds: the terms it talks about, and the things that actually happened in it.

## Added

- Concepts: a browsable index of the topics, people, companies and products your archive talks about. Pick a term to see every conversation that mentions it, and open one straight at the message the term was found in. It is built entirely on your machine, with no model and no network call.
- Moments: an index of what happened rather than what was discussed. Decisions made, advice given, requirements set, conclusions reached, each quoted from the message it happened in and openable at that message. An X-Ray view lays a conversation's moments out in order and shows what superseded, refined, resolved or contradicted what, across conversations. Indexing uses the OpenAI key you added for search, runs only when you ask for it, and tells you the cost first.
- Import a transcript by hand, from Settings. A VTT or SRT file, or pasted text, becomes an ordinary conversation you can read, search and index like any other. It closes the gap where a recording was deleted at the vendor before anything ever captured it.
- Pin or unpin a conversation at its source from the Reader, for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Copilot and Wave.
- Folders from Wave now sync into your library.
- Sources you never use can be hidden from the sidebar, without changing anything about what syncs.
- The Sync page gains a Select All button, and its status dots are half again as large.

## Improved

- Ladder search and Ask your archive are ordinary features now. There is nothing to switch on first.
- The sidebar reads as three groups and is the same list on every page, so a row is never missing just because of the page you are on. Extensions and Settings moved down to the footer, above Help.
- Gemini replies are stored as Markdown, so lists, bold, code and tables survive into the Reader.
- Pinning and deleting at the source report their progress and their outcome in one status card, instead of a message that arrives before the work has finished.
- Pinning and deleting keep working after a restart, instead of failing until the next sync has run.
- A Copilot conversation inside a project now explains why it cannot be pinned, rather than trying and failing. Copilot has no pin for those conversations at all.

## Fixed

- A browser tab that had quietly stopped responding no longer reports itself as a sign-in problem.
- Moments no longer stop partway through a long conversation.

## Removed

- The Experimental switch at the bottom of Settings is gone. Everything it used to gate now ships on.

Your projects and folders from Claude, Grok, Perplexity, and Copilot now sync into your library.

## Added

- Projects and folders now sync from Claude, Grok (Projects), Perplexity (Spaces), and Copilot, joining ChatGPT. Conversations appear under their folder, and a folder deleted on the source never deletes your saved conversations.
- Copilot conversations inside a project are now captured at all: Copilot only lists them inside the project, so earlier versions never saw them.
- The sync view shows a dedicated projects step with live counts, and Sync History gains a Projects column.

## Improved

- Copilot now syncs only in browsers that can actually read it. Microsoft Edge blocks extensions on copilot.microsoft.com, so those doomed attempts are skipped instead of failing every run.
- The New Chat button moved from the sidebar into the top right of the chats page.

## Fixed

- Ask your archive no longer fails with "reached its round limit": the search now wraps up with its best answer from the evidence it gathered.

A calmer, more consistent look across the app in both themes, and Claude Code's on-disk sessions now sync as their own lane.

## Added

- Claude Code and Claude Cowork conversations stored on this computer now sync as their own "This computer" lane beside the browser lanes, with its own badge on the Sync page, its own rows in the live view and Sync History, and its own counts. Session files are read directly from disk, no browser window needed.
- Sync page sources are now compact badges with a status dot. Hovering shows the stored conversation count and last synced time; right-clicking a source with stored data offers to remove its local copy.

## Improved

- A visual refresh across every page in both themes: flat surfaces with hairline borders replace gradients, glows, and blur; a single refined accent covers the primary action, active navigation, focus, and links; typography is calmer; status colors are softer tints. Light mode now sits on a near-white background with white cards. The website matches.
- Source names on cards, list rows, and the Files page read in quiet text while the colored source mark carries identity, keeping busy pages readable.
- While a sync runs, every row in the live view leads with the source's own tinted glyph, so a glance shows which source is being worked on.

A Files page that gathers every attachment across your chats in one place, and a simpler, more informative sidebar.

## Added

- A Files page, sitting between Projects and Usage in the sidebar. It lists every file across your whole archive: the ones you attached to prompts and the ones the chats produced in their replies, newest conversation first, each row showing where the file came from. A search box covers file names and conversation titles, and one filter chip per file type (with counts) makes "show me every PDF" a single click. The sidebar's source rows narrow the list in place, exactly as they do for your chats, and newly captured files appear while a sync runs without leaving the page.
- Every file offers two ways to open it: inside ChatsRecall, with the conversation opened right at the message that carries the file, or on the original chat page in a connected browser, scrolled to that message and highlighted. ChatsRecall stores file names and types, never the file contents, so opening a file always means finding it where it lives.

## Improved

- The Sync row in the sidebar now shows when the last sync finished ("5m ago") right on the row, replacing the small status line that used to sit at the bottom of the sidebar. While a sync runs, the familiar activity ring takes its place.
- Help is now a labeled row in the sidebar footer instead of a bare icon, and the Help dialog is more focused: open the Help page or replay onboarding from the beginning. The extension setup guide on its own is still available from Settings.
- The dark mode switch moved to Settings, under a new Appearance section, instead of a small icon at the bottom of the sidebar. The choice still applies everywhere and is remembered between launches.

Experimental search upgrades you can switch on, sync history that tells your browsers apart, and an early access point for AI tools.

## Added

- An Experimental features switch in Settings. It gathers still-settling capabilities in one place: the new Ladder search engine lives behind it, and the agent search button, previously always visible, now lives there too. With the switch off, nothing about the app changes.
- Ladder search (experimental): a second search engine you can flip to right inside the search field. When an exact match comes up empty, it progressively loosens the query (all terms, word variants, related concepts, soundalikes, partial matches) and stops at the first rung that finds enough, labeling every result page with how it matched. A sort control picks newest first or best match. Classic stays the default and is unchanged.
- An early access point for connecting AI tools to your archive: a local, read-only interface (REST and MCP) that listens only on your own machine, with per-tool tokens, scopes, daily quotas, and an audit log that never records message content. For advanced users for now: tokens are created from the command line until a proper in-app page arrives.

## Improved

- Sync History now tells your browsers apart. When more than one browser syncs the same source, the run shows one row per source with a small status badge per browser; clicking the row expands each browser's own result. If one browser fails while another succeeds, the row shows an amber warning instead of a red failure.

## Fixed

- After a large database upgrade on first launch, the app could open to an empty library until restarted. It now reloads itself when the upgrade finishes instead of accepting emptiness as an answer.

Pages open instantly while a sync runs, sync activity lives on the Sync row, and the new website Help page is one click away.

## Added

- A Help page on the ChatsRecall website with answers to common questions about setup, syncing, and your data, plus an Open Help page button in the app's Help & Support dialog that takes you straight there.
- A sync activity indicator on the Sync row of the sidebar: while a sync runs, a small orange ring appears at the right edge of the row, or on the corner of the sync button when the sidebar is collapsed. It is visible from every page of the app.

## Improved

- The status line in the sidebar's bottom corner now shows when your library last synced on every page. The conversation Reader, Extensions, and New Chat pages used to always say "Local".
- The search field shows a quiet accent border when focused instead of a thick outline ring.
- The Help & Support dialog closes with an X in its corner and fits its actions on one line.

## Fixed

- Opening a page while a sync was running could show a blank window for a second or two before anything appeared. Pages now show immediately and fill in as their content loads.

## Removed

- The orange "Syncing" pill in the sidebar's bottom corner. The Sync row's activity ring replaces it.

Blank conversations now fill in reliably, duplicate accounts are repaired, and Claude Code sessions show their files.

## Added

- Claude Code sessions now capture file attachments: images pasted into a prompt and files the agent created or edited. File names and types only; file contents are never read. Sessions saved before this update gain their files automatically on an upcoming sync.
- A Select all / Unselect all button on the Sync page flips every source switch at once.
- A conversation whose transcript is not saved yet now explains itself in the Reader: still queued, tried a few times so far, or given up with the recorded reason, instead of a bare "No messages".

## Improved

- Sync runs now rotate which source goes first, so every source gets its fair share of long runs.
- Automatic transcript backfill focuses on your most recent 18 months. Older conversations stay in your library, and a Full Refresh sync fetches them on request.

## Fixed

- A few unsaveable conversations could silently freeze the entire transcript backlog behind them; large backlogs of blank conversations now fill in over successive syncs (most visible on Perplexity).
- A sign-in hiccup during sync could create a duplicate "default" account holding an empty copy of your library (seen with Wave meetings). This no longer happens, and existing duplicates are folded back into the real account automatically, keeping the newest content and any pins.
- Scrolling the library no longer occasionally shows the same conversation twice.
- The minimized browser window a sync uses is now closed reliably after the run ends.

Decide which sources fill your sidebar, and a temporary change of source icons.

## Added

- Pick which sources appear in the sidebar. A new button next to the SOURCES label opens a picker where you turn sources on or off. Hidden sources keep syncing, their conversations stay under All Sources, and search still finds them; only the sidebar row is hidden.
- The onboarding tour has a new step that introduces the sources list and the visibility picker.

## Improved

- The sidebar starts with six everyday sources visible (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, and Copilot). The rest can be turned on from the picker at any time. Nothing about your saved conversations changes.
- The source icons across the app have been temporarily changed to a new set.

Read AI meetings now show up in your library.

## Fixed

- Read AI meetings were being saved but never shown: sync reported them as saved, yet the library and its counts left them out because Read AI was missing from the list of sources the library displays. Read AI meetings now appear in the library like every other source, including everything synced before this update, with no re-sync needed.
- The Usage page now includes Read AI alongside your other sources.

Read AI meetings now capture their full content, and scheduled syncs clean up after themselves instead of leaving a stray browser window open.

## Fixed

- Read AI meetings were coming through nearly empty: summaries were blank, the conversation itself was missing, and meetings with nothing captured kept being retried on every sync without ever finishing. Read AI sends its data in a different shape than ChatsRecall expected. ChatsRecall now reads what Read AI actually sends, so meeting summaries and everything that was said are captured again.
- Long sync runs could leave a minimized browser window behind when the browser briefly lost its connection to ChatsRecall partway through, and that window then stayed open forever. ChatsRecall now remembers any window it could not close and quietly closes it once the browser reconnects, after checking that the window is still only showing sync pages.

## Improved

- Sync history is clearer when Read AI cannot be reached: if the browser connector is too old for Read AI (0.1.5 or newer is needed), the sync now says exactly that instead of reporting an empty result, and when ChatsRecall cannot tell whether you are signed in to a source, the message now includes the reason.

Opening ChatsRecall while it is already running now brings back the window you already have instead of starting a second copy.

## Fixed

- Launching ChatsRecall from the Start menu while it was already running used to start a second copy of the app, with its own tray icon. The copies then competed for the browser connection and the conversation archive, which could quietly break live capture and make syncs fail. A second launch now simply brings the existing window to the front.

## Improved

- Opening ChatsRecall while it is hidden in the system tray now reopens its window right away, the same as clicking the tray icon.

Search results can now open the original page at the exact message, a sync walks all your sources through one tab per browser, and the browser extension updates itself without a restart.

## Added

- Open a search result right at the message that matched. Choose "open in browser" on a result and the original page scrolls to that message, outlines it, and paints your search terms, even when the site loads older messages lazily or collapses long ones. Results from sessions that live only on this computer, such as Claude Code and Cowork, open in the reader as before.
- The Extensions page now shows the version each connected browser extension is running and points out when a newer one is available.

> **Early preview:** opening a conversation at the exact message is brand new and not finished yet. Some sites may scroll to the wrong spot, skip the highlight, or take a moment to settle; the conversation itself still opens normally. Support is being verified site by site, and highlighting works best with browser extension 0.1.6. Older extensions fall back to a simpler locator that can miss on some pages.

## Improved

- Sync now opens a single window per connected browser and moves through your sources in one tab, instead of piling up tabs as it goes.
- The library remembers your place. Coming back from a conversation returns you to the same spot in the list, per filter.
- The browser extension (0.1.6) applies Chrome Web Store updates on its own at the next quiet moment, instead of waiting for a full browser restart.

## Fixed

- The browser chooser for Google AI Mode only offers browsers that can actually open it, and when none of them can, the message names what is missing instead of failing with a generic error.

## Removed

- Google AI Mode in Chrome. AI Mode searches, sync, and New Chat now always use another connected browser, such as Edge, with extension 0.1.3 or newer.

Read AI meetings join your library, search results stop drowning in pasted code, and a sync with two browsers connected reads as one clean list of sources.

## Added

- Sync Read AI meetings into your library. Each meeting arrives with its summary, action items, key questions, and who said what. Read AI appears on the Sync page with its switch off until you opt in.
- The desktop app can now pair with more than one extension build at a time, so a beta or test copy of the browser extension can connect alongside the one from the Chrome Web Store.

> **Compatibility note:** Read AI sync needs browser extension 0.1.5. If you turn the switch on before your extension updates, sync reports a sign-in problem until the update arrives.

## Improved

- Search now focuses on what was said, not on pasted code. Long code blocks no longer flood results for a common identifier, while short snippets such as error messages and one-line commands, plus inline code, stay searchable.
- Updating to this version rebuilds the search index once. The rebuild is fast even on large libraries, and if it needs more than a moment the app shows a progress window with a time estimate instead of a blank screen.
- Extensions running an older version are described in plain language on the Extensions page and in the browser chooser: connected and fully working, with the browser name arriving once the extension updates. No more "Legacy connector" labels or raw connector codes.

## Fixed

- With more than one browser connected, a running sync no longer lists every source twice. Each source is now a single row that marks each browser's progress with its own check, spinner, or cross, and expands to show per-browser accounts, counts, and any errors.
